journal.text: Fluid leakage and cramping during exercise.

rules.label: Warning signs in pregnancy
rules.text: Bleeding, fluid leakage, regular painful contractions, chest pain, persistent breathlessness, dizziness: stop now and call her obstetric team.

rules.label: Lying flat
rules.text: Lightheaded lying flat: sit her up or roll her to her left side; use an incline.

brief.situation: You are a personal trainer. Jess Moreno, 31 (a fictional client), is 24 weeks pregnant and wants to keep training. She was very active before pregnancy.
handover: Trainers program and supervise exercise; pregnancy complications go to her obstetric team.
Her midwife's labor and delivery triage line is saved on her phone.
howItWorks: Each task takes time: choose it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes.
The screen shows the client, your read-outs and findings, the plan and the rules that apply now.
When you end the session you write the record and explain your reasoning.

safetyNote: Teaching case for exam practice; fictional client. Not medical advice.

writeup.question: For her record: how you built today's session for pregnancy, what happened and what you did.

parts.label: The session
parts.criteria: Cleared, uncomplicated, previously active: continue moderate exercise with modifications: talk-test intensity, no prolonged lying flat (incline), no Olympic lifts or fall-risk moves, avoid heat; stopping all exercise is not the advice.
parts.modelAnswer: She is cleared and was active, so we kept training at a talk-test effort, swapped the flat bench for an incline and dropped the power cleans.

parts.label: Warning sign
parts.criteria: Fluid leakage with cramping at 24 weeks is a warning sign: stop at once, call labor and delivery triage now, arrange transport; never 'probably Braxton Hicks' or finish the cool-down.
parts.modelAnswer: Fluid and cramping at 24 weeks: I stopped her at once and we called labor and delivery triage together; her partner drove her in.

expertPath.text: Read the clearance; a modified session: talk-test effort, incline bench, no Olympic lifts or fall-risk moves.
Fluid and cramping: stop at once, sit her down, call labor and delivery triage with her; her partner drives.
A full record with the times.

calledIn.headline: Modified, stopped, called
calledIn.body: Pregnancy changes the program, not the habit. And fluid leakage or cramping is a stop sign and a call, not a cool-down.

gaps.headline: Called, with gaps
gaps.body: Check the program (modified for pregnancy, no lying flat) and how fast you stopped and called.

noExercise.headline: Not 'no exercise'
noExercise.body: A cleared, uncomplicated pregnancy is a reason to modify training, not to stop it.

pushed.headline: A warning sign is a stop sign
pushed.body: Fluid with cramping at 24 weeks is not Braxton Hicks to train through.

sentHome.headline: Call now, not later
sentHome.body: The warning signs mean calling her obstetric team at once, not finishing the session and waiting.

scoring.modelReasoning: Cleared, uncomplicated and previously active: keep her training with modifications (moderate effort by the talk test, no prolonged lying flat, no Olympic lifts or fall-risk activities, avoid heat). Lightheaded lying flat: sit her up or onto her left side. Fluid leakage with cramping is a warning sign: stop at once, call labor and delivery triage with her and arrange transport; do not train through it or send her home to watch it. Record the times.
